slide.title: intent.md · how we use it
slide.subtitle: Draft together in Proof. Approve as a squad. Commit the agreed intent to GitLab.

cards.title: WRITE TOGETHER
cards.body: Use a squad-owned Proof document for what, why, success criteria and boundaries. Mark unknowns OPEN.

cards.title: REVIEW WITH AN AGENT
cards.body: Ask for comments and suggestions. A named human accepts or rejects each proposal.

cards.title: AGREE AND COMMIT
cards.body: Approved Markdown goes to intent.md in GitLab, with Proof link, revision and reviewer. CLAUDE.md points to it.

steps: 5 min individually: draft what, why, success and boundaries.
5 min together: combine in one squad-owned Proof document.
5 min agent review: request comments and suggestions; review manually if agent access is unavailable.
5 min human decision: accept or reject proposals, copy approved Markdown to intent.md and prepare a GitLab merge request.
slide.expected: One reviewed intent.md, a Proof document link and revision, and a named reviewer on the GitLab merge request.
slide.check: Every participant can explain the intent. The repository copy matches the approved Proof text; unresolved proposals stay OPEN.
slide.prompt: Read our Proof draft. Suggest clearer scope, missing success criteria and one positive and one negative scenario. Keep unknowns OPEN. Explain each suggestion. Do not accept your own suggestions or change the approved repository files.
slide.notes:
Run this 20-minute sequence within the existing intent exercise, not as added agenda time. Guide: https://github.com/RyanLisse/aetherlink-agent-lab/blob/main/docs/proof-workflow.md . Use hosted Proof; create a separate document per squad. Agent writes require scoped access configured outside the repository. Use suggestions, with human approval. Sync is manual. At recap use Proof to discuss results, blockers and next owner; copy approved outcomes to progress.md. Never publish credential-bearing share links. Use synthetic training content.

Volledige kaarttekst (van de slide gehaald, hier voor de facilitator):
• AGREE AND COMMIT: Copy approved Markdown to intent.md in GitLab. Record the Proof link, revision and reviewer. CLAUDE.md explicitly points to intent.md.

• THE SECURITY EXAMPLE: Security teams are sized for human output. When agents multiply code, the review queue builds or code ships under-reviewed. A regulated organisation accepts neither, so the checks must keep pace with the agents.
